why: I checked the problem field and every expect line. The problem field only says what is wrong: index.js exports capitalize, slugify and truncate, none of them pads, and the README "has a section for capitalize(s) and one for truncate(s, n), but none for slugify". It names no fix. The expect lines describe behaviour you can observe from outside. The request itself requires the padLeft name and the 42 -> 00042 example. The other lines set results for number input, inputs already at the width, the space default, the README headings and npm test. None of them names an implementation technique or an internal helper. The fix choices go under assumptions instead: modelling the signature on String.prototype.padStart, converting input with String() and the `## name(...)` section format. The space default is a design choice the request doesn't make, but it sets the public behaviour, not how to build it.
